title: Embedded Software Developer (Space Domain) for Cybersecurity
description:
Embedded Software Developer (Space Domain) for Cybersecurity
Join the architects of e-Estonia and digital societies all over the world.
📍 Tallinn / Tartu, Estonia
We are looking for a Embedded Software Developer to join a cross-functional team building a cyber security module for spacecraft on commercial space hardware and a commercial RTOS. You'll work daily with the Product Owner, Product Analyst, Space Systems Integrator, and Test Engineer from early discovery through flight.
You own the onboard software. Design and build flight-grade software around proven algorithms: data paths, drivers, fault-tolerance/fail-safe behaviour, and a long-term update mechanism for an untouchable device.
Your main responsibilities will include
Designing and building the module's onboard software for resource-constrained hardware under real-time constraints, incl. porting the proprietary algorithms to the target module and RTOS
Designing and building the traffic interception and filtering data paths inside and below the OS network stack, and the bus drivers and protocol layers beneath it (CAN, MIL-STD-1553, SpaceWire, Ethernet, CCSDS added as the product grows), built to the Integrator's interface control documents
Implementing fault tolerance as product behaviour
Building the on-orbit update and configuration mechanism
Applying standards-aligned development practices throughout: requirements traceability, design documentation, configuration management, formal code review, and static analysis
Building and maintaining developer-side tooling and working directly with the OS and hardware vendors on BSP issues, driver defects, and performance problems
As a successful candidate, you must have
3+ years of production embedded software experience in C, C++, Ada, or Rust on resource-constrained hardware with real-time constraints
Prior experience in a standards- and regulations-driven environment
Real-time operating system experience used in earnest VxWorks, RTEMS, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or an in-house RTOS
A solid grounding in low-level networking device drivers, protocol stacks, and how data moves through them
Fault tolerance and resilience design experience in safety-critical systems, watchdog architectures, graceful degradation, safe mode design, and recovery strategies
Disciplined development practices: requirements traceability, configuration management, formal code review; static analysis and on-target unit testing are a plus
Hardware fluency - comfort reading schematics and datasheets, using an oscilloscope and logic analyzer, debugging at the hardware-software boundary
Comfort working day-to-day in a cross-functional product team alongside non-engineers
You will stand out by having any of the following:
Direct experience with spacecraft or satellite software: flight software, onboard data handling, or ground segment integration in a real programme context
Familiarity with the communication constraints of the space environment - intermittent contact windows, link budgets, data prioritisation under bandwidth limits, or CCSDS protocol knowledge
A bus or network technology you have implemented or substantially modified yourself: CAN, MIL-STD-1553, SpaceWire, Ethernet, or similar
Experience designing software update and configuration systems for deployments that cannot be patched on demand
Real-time performance engineering on RTOS: ensuring deterministic, bounded worst-case execution (DMA, cache management, interrupt handling, memory management)
Background in cybersecurity or security instrumentation or curiosity about the cybersecurity domain and willingness to grow into it is what matters
Technical leadership or mentorship experience on embedded teams working in regulated environments

title: Space Systems Integrator for Cybersecurity
description:
Space Systems Integrator for Cybersecurity
Join the architects of e-Estonia and digital societies all over the world.
📍 Tallinn / Tartu, Estonia
We are looking for a Space Systems Integrator to join a cross-functional product team building a cyber security module for spacecraft. Our primary target is mid-LEO Earth observation, science missions, commercial constellations.
You will be the team's expert on how spacecrafts are put together, across mission classes from CubeSats to large platforms, and on the buses, redundancy schemes, and architectural patterns our customers live with. You will join before the baseline exists.
Your first job is to set it: the buses we commit to, the interface behaviours we guarantee, the way the module participates in a customer's redundancy scheme. These are decisions the product will live with for years.
Your main responsibilities will include
Writing and owning the interface control documents, integration guides, and reference architectures that customers' integration engineers build to
Acting as design authority for everything observable at the connector i.e. interface behaviour, timing, bus configuration
Specifying and validating spacecraft-side simulation and test configurations with the Test Automation Engineer
Advising customers on placement: how the module fits their redundancy, fault-handling, and timing architectures
Owning the system-level technical relationship with the hardware vendor
Engaging early in discovery to surface system-level risks and options the rest of the team may not see
Supporting customers through integration - pre-sales consultation, integration reviews, and debugging at the spacecraft level when needed
Directing customer integration experience back into the product
As a successful candidate, you must have
Direct, hands-on spacecraft experience, i.e contribution to the architecture, integration, or operation of at least one real spacecraft that flew or was built to fly (coursework, simulation, and pure research roles do not meet this bar on their own)
Architectural breadth across spacecraft scales - practical familiarity with how nanosats, smallsats, and larger platforms are architected, where they differ, and what each demands of onboard components
Genuine working depth on several onboard buses and protocols, such as Time-Triggered Ethernet, standard Ethernet, SpaceWire, CAN, UART/RS-422/485, I²C/SPI, MIL-STD-1553, CCSDS Space Packet Protocol - meaning how they are used, configured, made redundant, and debugged on real vehicles, with test equipment in hand
Experience with spacecraft redundancy architectures and how onboard components participate in them
Systems engineering rigour - requirements decomposition and traceability, technical budgets, margin management; familiarity with NASA NPR 7120/7123 and the SE Handbook, ECSS-E-ST-10 / M-ST-10, or equivalents
The communication skills to explain and defend interface decisions to external engineering teams, and to write clear and precise documentation
You will stand out by having any of the following:
Direct customer integration experience - application engineering, field engineering, or supplier-side integration support on a flight programme
Production embedded development skill in C, C++, or Rust - letting you prototype reference integrations and bus emulations, and contribute directly to the testbench rather than only specifying it; genuinely differentiating, not required
